note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Fever and profuse sweating for 7 days.
- Associated symptoms: Generalized myalgia/aching, nausea with reduced oral intake, fatigue, night sweats, alternating hot and cold sensations; reports being "hot and sweaty" currently.
- Absent symptoms: No cough, no sore throat, no ear pain, no diarrhoea, no neck stiffness, no new rash, no joint swelling/tenderness, no urinary symptoms.
- Context: Returned from travel to Vietnam 4 weeks ago with rural exposure (trekking, cycling through countryside/farmland). Took malaria prophylaxis but cannot recall the drug name; believes it was a daily regimen and may have taken an additional agent “on top of the first” (uncertain).

Past Medical History:
- Chronic low back pain — under physiotherapy for posture/strengthening.
- History of headaches/migraines related to screen use and weather changes.
- Medications:
  - Seroxat (paroxetine) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Over-the-counter paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient reports taking recommended doses).
  - Over-the-counter ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient reports taking recommended doses).
- Allergies: Pollen (hay fever). No drug allergies reported.
- Social/occupational: Works as a nurse; non-smoker; moderate alcohol use; exercises moderately several times per week.
- Immunizations: Patient reports being up to date with occupational vaccinations (including hepatitis B).

Physical Examination:
- No formal examination documented during this consultation.
- Reported/observed findings from history:
  - Subjective fever and diaphoresis.
  - Generalized myalgia and nausea.
  - Alert and oriented (no altered mental status reported).
- Relevant negatives by history:
  - No respiratory symptoms (no cough, no sore throat).
  - No ear pain.
  - No gastrointestinal diarrhoea.
  - No neck stiffness, no rash.
  - No urinary symptoms or dysuria.
  - No focal joint swelling or new focal neurological deficits reported.

Impression:
- Fever of 7 days after recent travel to Vietnam — infectious etiology suspected; malaria is an important differential to exclude given travel history and ongoing fever.

Management Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face clinical assessment in clinic for physical examination.
- Request blood investigations to include:
  - Thick and thin blood films for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers and routine blood tests (as indicated by examining clinician). (Specific lab panels not fully detailed in transcript.)
- Administrative: Doctor will message admin to book patient into central London clinic; patient instructed to call the number in consultation notes to be scheduled.
- Alternative: Attend local Emergency Department/A&E if unable to attend clinic.
- Work advice: Advised not to return to work until this is investigated/resolved.
- Further management to be determined after clinical examination and test results.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with 7 days of fever, night sweats, generalized myalgia and nausea after returning from rural travel in Vietnam 4 weeks ago. Malaria and other infectious causes are a concern. Plan is same-day clinic assessment with blood tests (including malaria films) and to avoid work until evaluated.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend the arranged clinic for immediate clinical examination and blood tests (including malaria thick and thin films).
- Do not go to work until evaluated and cleared.
- If unable to get to the clinic, present to a local A&E and show the consultation notes.

Next Steps:
- Patient to call the booking number in the consultation notes to be scheduled for clinic today (patient agreed to come into central London).
- Clinic clinician to perform examination and determine urgency/extent of blood tests; laboratory testing to include thick and thin malaria films and inflammatory markers as indicated.
- Review results and plan further management based on examination and lab findings.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements: No documented vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, oxygen saturation), no documented physical examination findings, no laboratory results, specific malaria prophylaxis name and dosing unknown, exact return date from travel not fully specified beyond "four weeks ago", Seroxat dose not documented.
- Internal conflicts: Patient reports taking malaria prophylaxis but is uncertain of the drug name; she stated it was "daily" and also said she took "another one on top of the first" — ambiguity regarding exact prophylaxis regimen.
- Transcript quality: Overall clear and comprehensible with occasional brief inaudible/repetitive phrases; sufficient for extraction of clinical information.
